sources.name: Hacker News
sources.title: Residential proxies detected on White House network

stories.headline: Security firm reports residential proxies on White House network
stories.dek: A blog post from threat intelligence outfit Layer3 Intel says residential proxy traffic was detected on the White House network.
stories.body:
Residential proxy traffic has been detected on the White House network, according to a report published by Layer3 Intel on its company blog on November 4.

The post, titled "Residential proxies detected on White House network," quickly climbed to the top of Hacker News, where it collected 930 points and 281 comments.

Residential proxies route internet traffic through IP addresses assigned to ordinary home or consumer connections. That makes the traffic look like it comes from regular users instead of data centers or commercial services. For defenders, spotting such traffic on a sensitive network is generally treated as a signal worth investigating.

Layer3 Intel's report is the sole account of the finding. The White House has not publicly responded to it, and no independent confirmation of the claim has been published. Details such as when the traffic was observed, how much there was, which systems were involved and who is responsible have not been established publicly.

Until more is known, the finding stands as one security firm's claim. The strong reaction on Hacker News reflects how much attention any suggestion of unusual traffic on a government network draws in the security community.
key_points: Layer3 Intel reports residential proxy traffic on the White House network
Report published November 4 on the company's blog
Story reached 930 points and 281 comments on Hacker News
No independent confirmation or White House response so far
stories.why_it_matters: Residential proxy traffic blends in with ordinary consumer connections, so reports like this are a reminder that IP reputation alone is a weak signal for network defenders.

cover.caption: Hacker News points for Layer3 Intel's White House report

sources.name: Ars Technica
sources.title: Hackers exploited iOS and Android flaws to infect phones

stories.headline: Suspected Russian spies used patched phone flaws to hack site visitors
stories.dek: Sekoia links the campaign to Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service, citing fake sites mimicking a US anniversary group and a London hotel.
stories.body:
Hackers possibly tied to the Kremlin exploited previously patched iOS and Android flaws to infect visitors of potentially hundreds of websites, Ars Technica reports. Security firm Sekoia assessed with "moderate to high confidence" that the attackers belong to Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service. Many targeted sites had links to the war in Ukraine.

Injected JavaScript profiled each visiting phone, then delivered a platform-specific payload. The payloads tried to steal browser cookies and, in some cases, Wi-Fi passwords and full device data.

One fake domain, america250[.]holiday, proxied america250.org, the site of a group marking 250 years of American independence. Sekoia says the site may have been a pretext for invitation-themed spear-phishing. Another, theowo[.]club, mimicked Raffles London at The OWO, a hotel near the UK Ministry of Defence and 10 Downing Street.
key_points: Sekoia ties the campaign to Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service with "moderate to high confidence."
Attackers used already-patched iOS and Android flaws to steal cookies, Wi-Fi passwords and device data.
Fake sites proxied america250.org and a London luxury hotel near key UK government buildings.

sources.name: TechRadar
sources.title: Harvard University reveals data breach exposed 851,000 accounts

stories.headline: Harvard breach exposed 851,000 email addresses, HIBP finds
stories.dek: Have I Been Pwned analyzed data ShinyHunters leaked after a 2025 vishing attack on Harvard's alumni and fundraising systems.
stories.body:
Data stolen from Harvard University in a November 2025 breach contains 851,000 unique email addresses, according to Have I Been Pwned (HIBP), TechRadar reports. HIBP says the leaked archive also holds "extensive profile information" on donors, alumni, parents and some faculty, staff and students, including names, dates of birth, phone numbers, postal addresses and social media profiles.

Harvard confirmed in late November 2025 that its Alumni Affairs and Development systems were compromised through a voice phishing attack. The university said Social Security numbers, passwords and payment card data were not exposed. The ShinyHunters extortion group claimed responsibility and, after negotiations broke down, leaked more than 1.1GB of documents in early February.

Harvard was the third university hit in weeks, after Princeton and the University of Pennsylvania, where ShinyHunters claimed data on about 1.2 million people.
key_points: HIBP counts 851,000 unique email addresses in the leaked Harvard data, plus detailed profile records.
Attackers got in through a voice phishing attack on Harvard's alumni and fundraising systems in November 2025.
ShinyHunters leaked more than 1.1GB of documents after talks with Harvard broke down.

sources.title: Ripple-65B Preview: U.S. Open-Weight SOTA on Agentic Coding

stories.headline: Ricursive releases Ripple-65B, claims top US open-weight coding score
stories.dek: The chip-design AI lab says its dense 65B model beats far larger US open models on TerminalBench 2.1 and cost $32 million to build.
stories.body:
Ricursive Intelligence has released Ripple-65B Preview, an open-weight language model the company says sets a new US open-weight high on agentic coding. By its own figures, the model scores 80.52 on TerminalBench 2.1, ahead of Reflection Beam 501B (80.1), Meta Muse Spark Open 816B (76.4) and NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B (56.4). The scores are the company's and have not been independently verified.

Ripple is a general-purpose variant of the model behind Ricursive's chip design platform. It is a dense Transformer rather than Mixture-of-Experts, pretrained on 12 trillion tokens with up to 1M tokens of context. The company says its small size lets it run on local hardware such as NVIDIA DGX Spark.

Ricursive puts its full R&D cost at $32 million, which it estimates is one-tenth that of the prior leader. The model is on Hugging Face, Together AI, GMI Cloud and OpenRouter.
key_points: Ricursive claims a TerminalBench 2.1 score of 80.52, beating much larger US open-weight models by its own measure.
Ripple-65B is a dense model trained on 12 trillion tokens with up to 1M context, built for a total R&D cost of $32 million, the company says.
Weights are on Hugging Face, with hosted access via Together AI, GMI Cloud and OpenRouter.

sources.title: OpenAI to acquire Pierre Computer Company

stories.headline: OpenAI to acquire Pierre Computer Company
stories.dek: The ChatGPT maker announced the planned deal on its website, with terms not disclosed in the announcement's headline.
stories.body:
OpenAI plans to acquire Pierre Computer Company, the company announced on its website on Wednesday, November 4.

The announcement, titled "OpenAI to acquire Pierre Computer Company," did not come with publicly detailed terms at the time of writing. The price, deal structure, closing timeline and the future of Pierre's products and staff remain unclear.

The news drew attention among developers. A Hacker News thread linking to the announcement collected 227 points and 69 comments.
key_points: OpenAI announced on November 4 that it plans to acquire Pierre Computer Company.
Price and other deal terms have not been made public.
The Hacker News thread on the deal reached 227 points and 69 comments.

featured.headline: Frostpunk drops 90 percent to €2.99 on Steam: Strong Buy
featured.body:
Frostpunk is down to €2.99 on Steam, 90 percent off its regular €29.99. Steam users rate it Very Positive. That combination of a deep cut, a solid rating and a price below a cup of coffee makes it one of the safest buys on today's list.

The deal runs until November 14 at 18:00 UTC, so there is time, but little reason to wait. It suits anyone who has had Frostpunk sitting on a wishlist, or a player looking for a well-reviewed game to fill the gap before the next big release. At this price, even a few evenings of play pay for it.

featured.headline: Borderlands 3 falls to €5.99, 90 percent off: Strong Buy
featured.body:
Borderlands 3 costs €5.99 on Steam, down 90 percent from its regular €59.99. Steam users rate it Very Positive. That is a cut of €54 on a full-priced game, the biggest absolute saving in today's deals.

The offer ends November 16 at 18:00 UTC, the latest end date on the list. Borderlands 2 is also 90 percent off at €2.99 until the same date, so series newcomers can pick up both for under €9. It is a strong buy for anyone who skipped Borderlands 3 at full price, and especially for players who want a game to share with friends.
